# This MiniCluster manifest is designed for running a LAMMPS ReaxFF simulation
# on a single AWS ARM-based CPU node in a Kubernetes cluster, managed by the Flux Operator.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Using a unique name to prevent collisions with previous experiments.
  name: lammps-reax-mc-3
  namespace: default
spec:
  # Number of pods (nodes) for the MiniCluster. Set to 1 as requested.
  size: 1

  # The main container specification that will run the HPC application.
  # The Flux Operator will inject flux and wrap the command.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      # The command to execute for the LAMMPS simulation.
      # This command will be wrapped by `flux run`.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
      # The launcher pod is managed by the Flux Operator, not this container.
      launcher: false
      # Always pull the image to ensure the latest version is used for the experiment.
      imagePullPolicy: Always
      # Resource requests and limits for AWS Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA).
      resources:
        requests:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"
        limits:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"

  # Flux Operator specific settings for managing the Flux Framework environment.
  flux:
    # Specify the architecture for the flux binaries since this runs on an ARM instance.
    arch: "arm"
    container:
      # Disable the flux-view sidecar container. The main application container
      # already has the necessary environment and flux will be installed into it.
      disable: true
      # Image for the flux-view container, required for ARM architecture.
      # Note: This image is not actually used when `disable` is true, but is
      # included here as per the explicit instructions.
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:arm-jammy

  # Logging settings for the Flux job.
  logging:
    # Fail the job on any error for stricter control during experiments.
    strict: true

  # Do not delete the pods after the job completes to allow for log inspection and debugging.
  cleanup: false

For the ReaxFF potential in LAMMPS, achieving perfect linear scaling is challenging due to the dynamic nature of bond re-formation and the complexity of charge equilibration, which increases communication overhead. A key principle of strong scaling is that as the number of processors increases for a fixed problem size, the sub-domain size (and thus the amount of computation) per processor decreases.
